322	// MARK: - The tap
323	
324	/// One tap's state: what it was built with, and everything it carries between
325	/// buffers.
326	///
327	/// Held by the tap through `MTAudioProcessingTapGetStorage`, retained on
328	/// creation and released in the finalize callback — the tap is a CF object
329	/// owned by the `AVMutableAudioMixInputParameters` it is set on, and this
330	/// object's life is exactly the tap's.
331	final class AudioTapContext {
332	    private let track: AudioTrackDSP
333	    /// Where this track's levels are published, on a metering (playback)
334	    /// build; nil on every export and on every rendered frame. Written on the
335	    /// audio thread with two relaxed atomic stores and nothing else — see
336	    /// `LevelMeter.swift` for why it is not the `NSLock` the rest of the app
337	    /// publishes across threads with.
338	    private let meter: LevelMeterSink?
339	    private var chain: AudioDSPChain?
340	    /// The channel base pointers, refilled per buffer. A stored array so no
341	    /// allocation happens on the audio thread.
342	    private var channels: [UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?] = []
343	    /// The rate `prepare` reported. Frames are turned into ticks with THIS
344	    /// and not with the timestamp's own timescale: the two happen to agree on
345	    /// both paths measured here, and only one of them is the contract.
346	    private var sampleRate: Ticks = 48000
347	    /// Where the last buffer ended, in composition ticks. Used when the tap
348	    /// reports no usable time — which the player's first callback after a
349	    /// start does — and to notice a seek.
350	    private var position: Ticks = 0
351	
352	    /// How far a buffer's start may be from where the last one ended before it
353	    /// is treated as a seek rather than as the next block. A tenth of a second
354	    /// is far longer than any buffer this path delivers (4096 frames is 85 ms
355	    /// at 48 kHz) and far shorter than any jump a scrub makes.
356	    private static let seekTolerance: Ticks = ReelTime.perSecond / 10
357	
358	    init(track: AudioTrackDSP, meter: LevelMeterSink?) {
359	        self.track = track
360	        self.meter = meter
361	    }
362	
363	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
364	        fatalError("AudioTapContext does not support NSCoder")
365	    }
366	
367	    /// `prepare`: the format is finally known, so the chain can size itself.
368	    /// Called again after every `unprepare`, so it replaces rather than adds.
369	    ///
370	    /// **The format is checked rather than assumed.** Both paths measured here
371	    /// hand a tap 32-bit float, non-interleaved, one `AudioBuffer` per channel
372	    /// — the format `AudioDSP` is written for. Nothing in the API promises
373	    /// that. If it is ever something else (interleaved, or fixed point) the
374	    /// chain is simply not built and the track passes through untouched:
375	    /// reading interleaved stereo as if it were one channel would apply the
376	    /// left gain to both and process half the buffer, which is a corrupted
377	    /// export rather than a missing feature. The METER is refused by the same
378	    /// guard and for the same reason — an interleaved buffer read as planar
379	    /// would meter half a channel — so a track in an unexpected format shows
380	    /// no level rather than a wrong one.
381	    ///
382	    /// `channels` being non-empty is what says the format was accepted; a
383	    /// metering-only track has no chain but still has that array, so
384	    /// everything that must not run in an unusable format is gated on it.
385	    func prepare(
386	        channelCount: Int, sampleRate: Double, maxFrames: Int,
387	        formatFlags: AudioFormatFlags, bitsPerChannel: UInt32
388	    ) {
389	        let float = formatFlags & kAudioFormatFlagIsFloat != 0
390	        let planar = formatFlags & kAudioFormatFlagIsNonInterleaved != 0
391	        guard float, planar, bitsPerChannel == 32, channelCount > 0 else {
392	            chain = nil
393	            channels = []
394	            meter?.clear()
395	            return
396	        }
397	        // No chain at all for a metering-only track: the compressor stage
398	        // alone allocates three buffers of `maxFrames`, and running it with no
399	        // settings would still be a multiply per sample per channel for a
400	        // track that asked for nothing.
401	        chain = track.isActive
402	            ? AudioDSPChain(
403	                channelCount: channelCount, sampleRate: sampleRate, maxFrames: maxFrames,
404	                usesNoiseReduction: track.usesNoiseReduction)
405	            : nil
406	        channels = Array(repeating: nil, count: channelCount)
407	        self.sampleRate = sampleRate >= 1 ? Ticks(sampleRate) : 48000
408	        position = 0
409	    }
410	
411	    func unprepare() {
412	        chain = nil
413	        channels = []
414	        meter?.clear()
415	    }
416	
417	    /// `process`: run the chain over one buffer of already-fetched audio.
418	    ///
419	    /// `time` is what `MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio` reported, which is
420	    /// invalid on the player's very first callback (measured) — hence the
421	    /// carried position.
422	    func process(
423	        _ bufferList: UnsafeMutablePointer<AudioBufferList>, frames: Int, time: CMTime,
424	        startOfStream: Bool
425	    ) {
426	        guard frames > 0, !channels.isEmpty else { return }
427	        let start = time.isNumeric ? CompositionBuilder.ticks(time) : position
428	        let list = UnsafeMutableAudioBufferListPointer(bufferList)
429	        let count = min(list.count, channels.count)
430	        guard count > 0 else { return }
431	
432	        if let chain = chain {
433	            // A seek, a loop or a fresh stream: the compressor's envelope and
434	            // the reducer's delay line belong to the position we just left.
435	            if startOfStream || abs(start - position) > Self.seekTolerance {
436	                chain.reset()
437	            }
438	
439	            // A buffer that straddles a cut is processed in runs, so a clip's
440	            // pan begins exactly at its own first sample rather than up to a
441	            // buffer early. The stages keep their state across the boundary —
442	            // they are track inserts, not per-clip effects.
443	            var offset = 0
444	            while offset < frames {
445	                let run = self.run(from: start + ticks(frames: offset), remaining: frames - offset)
446	                guard run.length > 0 else { break }
447	                for index in 0..<count {
448	                    channels[index] = list[index].mData?
449	                        .assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self).advanced(by: offset)
450	                }
451	                channels.withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer { pointers in
452	                    chain.process(
453	                        UnsafeMutableBufferPointer(rebasing: pointers[0..<count]),
454	                        frames: run.length, params: run.dsp)
455	                }
456	                offset += run.length
457	            }
458	        }
459	        position = start + ticks(frames: frames)
460	
461	        // AFTER the chain, and over the whole buffer rather than per run: what
462	        // the meter is asked for is the level this track hands the mix, and
463	        // the pan and the compressor have moved it. The run loop above left
464	        // `channels` pointing into the LAST run, so the base pointers are
465	        // written back before the sink reads them.
466	        guard let meter = meter else { return }
467	        for index in 0..<count {
468	            channels[index] = list[index].mData?.assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self)
469	        }
470	        channels.withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer { pointers in
471	            meter.measure(
472	                UnsafeMutableBufferPointer(rebasing: pointers[0..<count]), count: count,
473	                frames: frames)
474	        }
475	    }
476	
477	    private func ticks(frames: Int) -> Ticks {
478	        Ticks(frames) * ReelTime.perSecond / sampleRate
479	    }
480	
481	    private func samples(_ ticks: Ticks) -> Int {
482	        let value = max(ticks, 0) * sampleRate / ReelTime.perSecond
483	        return value > Ticks(Int.max) ? Int.max : Int(value)
484	    }
485	
486	    /// The longest run from `at` over which one clip's settings hold, and
487	    /// those settings. A gap between clips is a run of inert samples rather
488	    /// than a stop, so the silence between two panned clips stays silence.
489	    private func run(from at: Ticks, remaining: Int) -> (length: Int, dsp: AudioClipDSP) {
490	        guard let index = span(covering: at) else {
491	            // Not inside any span: run to whichever comes first, the next
492	            // span's start or the end of the buffer.
493	            guard let next = track.spans.first(where: { $0.start > at })?.start
494	            else { return (remaining, .inert) }
495	            return (min(remaining, max(1, samples(next - at))), .inert)
496	        }
497	        let span = track.spans[index]
498	        return (min(remaining, max(1, samples(span.end - at))), span.dsp)
499	    }
500	
501	    /// Binary search rather than a carried cursor: a scrub jumps anywhere, and
502	    /// `log n` with no state beats `n` with state that a seek invalidates.
503	    private func span(covering at: Ticks) -> Int? {
504	        var low = 0
505	        var high = track.spans.count - 1
506	        while low <= high {
507	            let middle = (low + high) / 2
508	            let span = track.spans[middle]
509	            if at < span.start {
510	                high = middle - 1
511	            } else if at >= span.end {
512	                low = middle + 1
513	            } else {
514	                return middle
515	            }
516	        }
517	        return nil
518	    }
519	}

521	/// Builds the `MTAudioProcessingTap` for one composition audio track.
522	enum AudioTap {
523	    /// nil when the track needs no processing AND is not being metered, or
524	    /// when MediaToolbox refuses to make a tap — in which case the track plays
525	    /// and exports unprocessed and unmetered, which is the old behaviour
526	    /// rather than a failed build.
527	    ///
528	    /// A `meter` alone is enough to earn a tap: a metering build wants a level
529	    /// from every audio track, including the ones no clip has asked anything
530	    /// of. That tap builds no chain and touches no sample — it fetches its
531	    /// source audio, hands it straight on, and measures it.
532	    static func make(for track: AudioTrackDSP?, meter: LevelMeterSink?) -> MTAudioProcessingTap? {
533	        let track = track ?? .inert
534	        guard track.isActive || meter != nil else { return nil }
535	        // Retained here, released in `finalize` (or below, if no tap is made):
536	        // the tap owns the context and outlives every Swift reference to it.
537	        let context = Unmanaged.passRetained(
538	            AudioTapContext(track: track, meter: meter)).toOpaque()
539	        var callbacks = MTAudioProcessingTapCallbacks(
540	            version: kMTAudioProcessingTapCallbacksVersion_0,
541	            clientInfo: context,
542	            init: { _, clientInfo, storageOut in storageOut.pointee = clientInfo },
543	            finalize: { tap in
544	                Unmanaged<AudioTapContext>
545	                    .fromOpaque(MTAudioProcessingTapGetStorage(tap)).release()
546	            },
547	            prepare: { tap, maxFrames, format in
548	                let context = Unmanaged<AudioTapContext>
549	                    .fromOpaque(MTAudioProcessingTapGetStorage(tap)).takeUnretainedValue()
550	                context.prepare(
551	                    channelCount: Int(format.pointee.mChannelsPerFrame),
552	                    sampleRate: format.pointee.mSampleRate, maxFrames: Int(maxFrames),
553	                    formatFlags: format.pointee.mFormatFlags,
554	                    bitsPerChannel: format.pointee.mBitsPerChannel)
555	            },
556	            unprepare: { tap in
557	                Unmanaged<AudioTapContext>
558	                    .fromOpaque(MTAudioProcessingTapGetStorage(tap))
559	                    .takeUnretainedValue().unprepare()
560	            },
561	            process: { tap, numberFrames, _, bufferListInOut, numberFramesOut, flagsOut in
562	                let context = Unmanaged<AudioTapContext>
563	                    .fromOpaque(MTAudioProcessingTapGetStorage(tap)).takeUnretainedValue()
564	                var timeRange = CMTimeRange()
565	                // The source audio must be fetched even when nothing will be
566	                // done to it: this call is what hands the buffer on.
567	                guard MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio(
568	                    tap, numberFrames, bufferListInOut, flagsOut, &timeRange,
569	                    numberFramesOut) == noErr
570	                else {
571	                    numberFramesOut.pointee = 0
572	                    return
573	                }
574	                // `MTAudioProcessingTapFlags` is a plain bit field, not an
575	                // `OptionSet`: the header declares it `uint32_t`.
576	                let startOfStream =
577	                    flagsOut.pointee & MTAudioProcessingTapFlags(
578	                        kMTAudioProcessingTapFlag_StartOfStream) != 0
579	                context.process(
580	                    bufferListInOut, frames: Int(numberFramesOut.pointee),
581	                    time: timeRange.start, startOfStream: startOfStream)
582	            })
583	
584	        var tap: MTAudioProcessingTap?
585	        guard MTAudioProcessingTapCreate(
586	            kCFAllocatorDefault, &callbacks, kMTAudioProcessingTapCreationFlag_PreEffects,
587	            &tap) == noErr
588	        else {
589	            // The context was retained for a tap that does not exist.
590	            Unmanaged<AudioTapContext>.fromOpaque(context).release()
591	            return nil
592	        }
593	        return tap
594	    }
595	}

144	// MARK: - Pan
145	
146	/// The pan law: constant power, normalised to unity at the centre.
147	///
148	/// **Why constant power.** Two uncorrelated channels sum by POWER, so a law
149	/// that keeps `L² + R²` constant is the one that holds perceived loudness
150	/// across the sweep; the linear law (`L = 1 - t`, `R = t`) drops 6 dB in the
151	/// middle and sounds like a dip as the clip crosses the centre.
152	///
153	/// **Why normalised to unity rather than to the edges.** The textbook
154	/// constant-power law puts 0.707 in both channels at the centre — a 3 dB cut
155	/// applied to every clip whose pan is 0, which is every clip in every project
156	/// that has ever been opened in this app. Multiplying the pair by √2 moves
157	/// the unity point to the centre instead, so pan 0 is EXACTLY a no-op
158	/// (`gains(0) == (1, 1)` is asserted, not hoped for) and the price is paid at
159	/// the extremes, where a hard-panned clip is 3 dB louder in the channel it
160	/// went to. That is the right trade for an editor: the common case is
161	/// transparent and the loud case is one the user chose.
162	///
163	/// **On a stereo clip this is a BALANCE.** Applying one gain to L and another
164	/// to R does not move a stereo image the way panning a mono source into a
165	/// stereo bus does; it leans it. That is what every editor's clip-level pan
166	/// does, and folding to mono first to get a "true" pan would throw away the
167	/// stereo the clip was recorded with.
168	///
169	/// **On a clip that asks for `mono` it is a TRUE pan**, and that is the
170	/// honest description rather than a special case: the fold runs at the head of
171	/// the Mix stage, immediately before this, so both channels hold the same
172	/// signal and leaning them moves one source between two speakers. It is also
173	/// why the fold cannot go after the pan — `(g_L·x + g_R·x)/2 = ((g_L+g_R)/2)·x`
174	/// is the same signal in both channels at every pan position, so the control
175	/// would degrade into a gain change and read as broken. A fold an enclosing
176	/// NEST clip asks for DOES run after this pan, and is not that case: it folds
177	/// the nest's mix, and flattening whatever panning happens inside the nest is
178	/// precisely what that means (`AudioDSPChain`).
179	///
180	/// **A mono composition track cannot be panned at all** — measured, not
181	/// assumed: a tap on a track whose source is mono is prepared with one
182	/// channel, and the upmix to stereo happens downstream of it. There is no
183	/// second channel to write to, so pan on such a clip is inaudible; see
184	/// `AudioDSPChain.process`.
185	enum AudioPanLaw {
186	    static func gains(_ pan: Double) -> (left: Float, right: Float) {
187	        guard pan.isFinite, pan != 0 else { return (1, 1) }
188	        let clamped = min(max(pan, -1), 1)
189	        // 0 … π/2 as the pan runs left … right.
190	        let theta = (clamped + 1) * Double.pi / 4
191	        return (Float(cos(theta) * 2.0.squareRoot()), Float(sin(theta) * 2.0.squareRoot()))
192	    }
193	}

197	/// A feed-forward peak compressor with a hard knee, channel-linked.
198	///
199	/// **Linked, not per channel.** The detector is the largest absolute sample
200	/// across the channels and one gain is applied to all of them. Compressing
201	/// each channel on its own detector makes the stereo image wander whenever
202	/// one side is louder, which is the classic way a compressor ruins a mix.
203	///
204	/// **One compressor per composition TRACK, not per clip.** A composition
205	/// audio track is a sequence of clips (§7.2) and this sits on it like a
206	/// channel-strip insert: the settings change at each cut, the envelope
207	/// carries across it. Restarting the envelope per clip would make every cut
208	/// audible as a jump in gain reduction.
209	///
210	/// The envelope is a one-pole smoother on the gain reduction in dB, which is
211	/// the standard shape: `attack` is how fast the reduction closes on a level
212	/// that just rose, `release` how fast it opens again.
213	final class AudioCompressorStage {
214	    /// Current gain reduction in dB, always ≥ 0. Persists across buffers.
215	    private var reductionDB: Float = 0
216	    /// The peak follower's state — see `processChunk`. Also persists.
217	    private var detectorState: Float = 0
218	    private let sampleRate: Double
219	    /// The linked detector and the per-sample gain, sized once.
220	    private let detector: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
221	    private let scratch: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
222	    private let gains: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
223	    private let capacity: Int
224	
225	    init(sampleRate: Double, maxFrames: Int) {
226	        self.sampleRate = sampleRate > 0 ? sampleRate : 48000
227	        capacity = max(1, maxFrames)
228	        detector = .allocate(capacity: capacity)
229	        scratch = .allocate(capacity: capacity)
230	        gains = .allocate(capacity: capacity)
231	        detector.initialize(repeating: 0, count: capacity)
232	        scratch.initialize(repeating: 0, count: capacity)
233	        gains.initialize(repeating: 1, count: capacity)
234	    }
235	
236	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
237	        fatalError("AudioCompressorStage does not support NSCoder")
238	    }
239	
240	    deinit {
241	        detector.deallocate()
242	        scratch.deallocate()
243	        gains.deallocate()
244	    }
245	
246	    /// Forgets the envelope and the follower. Called when playback restarts,
247	    /// so a paused-then-resumed preview does not open with the reduction the
248	    /// last buffer left.
249	    func reset() {
250	        reductionDB = 0
251	        detectorState = 0
252	    }
253	
254	    /// A one-pole coefficient for a time constant in seconds. Zero seconds
255	    /// means "instantly", which is a legitimate setting (a brick-wall attack)
256	    /// and must not divide by zero.
257	    private func coefficient(_ seconds: Double) -> Float {
258	        guard seconds > 0 else { return 1 }
259	        return Float(1 - exp(-1 / (seconds * sampleRate)))
260	    }
261	
262	    /// Compresses `frames` samples in place across `count` channels.
263	    ///
264	    /// `settings` of nil means this clip asks for no compression: the target
265	    /// reduction is 0 but the envelope still RELEASES toward it, so a cut from
266	    /// a compressed clip to an uncompressed one opens up over the last
267	    /// clip's release time instead of stepping.
268	    func process(
269	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, count: Int,
270	        frames: Int, settings: AudioCompressorSettings?
271	    ) {
272	        guard frames > 0, count > 0 else { return }
273	        // `maxFrames` is what `prepare` promised, not a guarantee: a buffer
274	        // bigger than the scratch is split rather than dropped, because
275	        // silently leaving audio unprocessed is the one outcome worth ruling
276	        // out.
277	        var offset = 0
278	        while offset < frames {
279	            let chunk = min(capacity, frames - offset)
280	            processChunk(channels, count: count, offset: offset, frames: chunk, settings: settings)
281	            offset += chunk
282	        }
283	    }
284	
285	    private func processChunk(
286	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, count: Int,
287	        offset: Int, frames: Int, settings: AudioCompressorSettings?
288	    ) {
289	        // The linked detector: |x| of the first channel, then the running
290	        // maximum against every other. Vectorised — this is two passes over
291	        // the buffer rather than a branch per sample per channel.
292	        var wrote = false
293	        for channel in 0..<count {
294	            guard let data = channels[channel] else { continue }
295	            if !wrote {
296	                vDSP_vabs(data + offset, 1, detector, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
297	                wrote = true
298	            } else {
299	                vDSP_vabs(data + offset, 1, scratch, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
300	                vDSP_vmax(detector, 1, scratch, 1, detector, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
301	            }
302	        }
303	        guard wrote else { return }
304	
305	        let thresholdDB = Float(settings?.thresholdDB ?? 0)
306	        let ratio = Float(settings?.ratio ?? 1)
307	        // How much of every dB above the threshold is given back. Ratio 1
308	        // (or no compressor at all) makes this 0 and the stage a pure makeup
309	        // gain, which is exactly what 1:1 means.
310	        let slope = ratio > 1 ? 1 - 1 / ratio : 0
311	        let makeupDB = Float(settings?.makeupDB ?? 0)
312	        let thresholdLinear = AudioDSP.gain(fromDecibels: thresholdDB)
313	        let attack = coefficient(settings?.attackSeconds ?? 0)
314	        let release = coefficient(settings?.releaseSeconds ?? 0)
315	        // The detector is a PEAK FOLLOWER — it jumps to each new peak and
316	        // falls back at the release rate — rather than the raw |x|. A naive
317	        // detector reads a waveform's own zero crossings as the level
318	        // collapsing, so the gain is modulated at twice the signal's
319	        // frequency: audible as distortion on anything low, and the reason a
320	        // sine measured through a textbook 3:1 lands a few tenths of a dB
321	        // shy of where the arithmetic says it should. The floor keeps a
322	        // zero-release setting from turning the follower back into |x|.
323	        let fall = Float(exp(-1 / (max(settings?.releaseSeconds ?? 0, 0.010) * sampleRate)))
324	
325	        for index in 0..<frames {
326	            detectorState = max(detector[index], detectorState * fall)
327	            let level = detectorState
328	            // The log is skipped entirely below the threshold, which is where
329	            // most samples of most material are.
330	            var target: Float = 0
331	            if slope > 0, level > thresholdLinear {
332	                let levelDB = 20 * log10f(max(level, AudioDSP.silenceFloor))
333	                target = (levelDB - thresholdDB) * slope
334	            }
335	            let coefficient = target > reductionDB ? attack : release
336	            reductionDB += (target - reductionDB) * coefficient
337	            gains[index] = AudioDSP.gain(fromDecibels: makeupDB - reductionDB)
338	        }
339	
340	        for channel in 0..<count {
341	            guard let data = channels[channel] else { continue }
342	            vDSP_vmul(data + offset, 1, gains, 1, data + offset, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
343	        }
344	    }
345	}

348	
349	/// Broadband noise reduction, one instance per channel: a short-time spectral
350	/// attenuator over a noise floor the signal itself is measured for.
351	///
352	/// **What it actually does**, spelled out so that neither this comment nor the
353	/// pane's label can overstate it. The signal is cut into 512-sample frames
354	/// every 128 samples and each is windowed and transformed. A per-bin estimate
355	/// of the background noise floor is tracked continuously. Each bin is then
356	/// multiplied by a Wiener gain — `SNR / (SNR + k)` — over a decision-directed
357	/// estimate of that bin's signal-to-noise ratio, with `k` the over-subtraction
358	/// factor the user's amount sets and a floor under the result so a suppressed
359	/// bin fades rather than vanishes. The frames are windowed again and
360	/// overlap-added back.
361	///
362	/// **It is not a gate, and the difference is the point.** Nothing here
363	/// compares a level with a threshold and decides between "signal" and
364	/// "silence": every bin of every frame keeps the fraction of itself that its
365	/// own SNR says is signal, so a quiet passage keeps its content and a steady
366	/// hiss is attenuated *underneath* speech rather than only between words. What
367	/// it cannot do is remove a noise that is not stationary — a door slam, a
368	/// cough — because nothing distinguishes those from the material.
369	///
370	/// **The noise estimate is continuous minimum tracking** (Doblinger's
371	/// recursive-minimum variant of Martin's minimum statistics): the smoothed
372	/// power in each bin is followed by a value that falls to it instantly and
373	/// rises back only slowly, so it settles on the floor the bin returns to
374	/// between sounds. That needs no noise print from the user and no silence at
375	/// the head of the clip. Its known cost is that a bin which is never quiet —
376	/// a long held note — is eventually read as noise; `minimumRise` is set for
377	/// that case and the decision-directed SNR carries the rest.
378	///
379	/// **Latency.** An STFT cannot see a sample's neighbours before they arrive,
380	/// so the output lags the input by one analysis window: 512 samples, 10.7 ms
381	/// at 48 kHz. Measured, not assumed: a tap's process callback cannot read
382	/// ahead — a second `MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio` inside one callback
383	/// returns the SAME audio again rather than the next block, so priming a
384	/// look-ahead is impossible. 10.7 ms is far inside every A/V sync tolerance
385	/// and applies only to a track some clip of which asks for noise reduction;
386	/// `AudioTap` keeps the stage running for the whole track once any clip on it
387	/// does, so the delay never changes at a cut.
388	final class AudioNoiseReductionStage {
389	    /// Analysis window, a power of two for `vDSP`'s radix-2 FFT.
390	    static let window = 512
391	    /// Hop: 75 % overlap, which is what a √Hann pair needs to add back up to
392	    /// a constant and is fine enough that a modified bin does not smear.
393	    static let hop = 128
394	
395	    private let log2n: vDSP_Length
396	    private let setup: FFTSetup
397	    private let half: Int
398	
399	    /// √Hann, used for BOTH analysis and synthesis (Griffin–Lim): windowing
400	    /// twice is what keeps a per-bin gain change from clicking at the frame
401	    /// edges.
402	    private let windowCurve: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
403	    /// Everything below is allocated once and reused every frame.
404	    private let history: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>      // last `window` inputs
405	    private let staging: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>      // this hop's inputs
406	    private let frame: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
407	    private let real: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
408	    private let imaginary: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>
409	    private let power: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>        // half + 1
410	    private let smoothed: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>     // half + 1
411	    private let minimum: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>      // half + 1
412	    private let binGain: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>      // half + 1
413	    /// Last frame's estimate of the CLEAN power per bin, which is what makes
414	    /// the a priori SNR below a decision-directed one rather than a raw
415	    /// per-frame ratio.
416	    private let cleaned: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>      // half + 1
417	    private let overlap: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>      // window
418	    /// The finished samples waiting to be handed back, as a plain FIFO with a
419	    /// read and a write index. It never holds more than two hops, and it is
420	    /// compacted on a push rather than shifted on a pop — a `memmove` per
421	    /// SAMPLE is what a naive queue costs here, and this runs on the audio
422	    /// thread.
423	    private let output: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>       // window + hop
424	    private var outputHead = 0
425	    private var outputTail = 0
426	    private var stagedCount = 0
427	    /// False until the first frame has been analysed. The tracker starts at
428	    /// that frame's own power rather than at zero: from zero it would take
429	    /// its whole rise constant to charge up to the noise floor, and until it
430	    /// did every bin would look like signal and nothing would be removed.
431	    private var primed = false
432	    /// The forward/inverse round trip's scale, times the overlap-add
433	    /// normalisation. Both are constants of the window and the hop, so they
434	    /// are folded into one multiply.
435	    private let scale: Float
436	
437	    /// Smoothing of the per-bin power before the minimum tracker sees it.
438	    private let powerSmoothing: Float = 0.7
439	    /// How fast the tracked minimum may rise back — the one number that
440	    /// decides whether a held note is mistaken for the room.
441	    ///
442	    /// The tracker FALLS instantly and rises at this rate, so an
443	    /// overestimate corrects itself within a few frames of quiet while an
444	    /// underestimate persists. That asymmetry says to be slow: 0.9999 per hop
445	    /// is about 27 s at 48 kHz. Measured on a one-second 700 Hz tone buried
446	    /// in white noise, 0.998 (1.4 s) took 12 dB off the tone and 0.9995 (5 s)
447	    /// took 10 dB, because the tracker climbed to the tone and the filter
448	    /// then read it as the floor; at 0.9999 the tone comes through within
449	    /// half a dB and the noise-only stretches still lose 13.
450	    private let minimumRise: Float = 0.9999
451	    private let minimumBias: Float = 0.96
452	    /// The tracked minimum reads low, because it is a minimum; the usual
453	    /// compensation for the bias of that estimator.
454	    private let noiseBias: Float = 1.5
455	    /// How much of the a priori SNR is carried from the previous frame's
456	    /// clean estimate. 0.98 is Ephraim and Malah's own figure, and it is what
457	    /// stops the gain from chattering bin by bin — the chatter IS musical
458	    /// noise.
459	    private let decisionDirected: Float = 0.98
460	
461	    init?() {
462	        var n = 1
463	        var bits: vDSP_Length = 0
464	        while n < Self.window {
465	            n <<= 1
466	            bits += 1
467	        }
468	        guard n == Self.window, let setup = vDSP_create_fftsetup(bits, FFTRadix(kFFTRadix2))
469	        else { return nil }
470	        self.setup = setup
471	        log2n = bits
472	        half = Self.window / 2
473	
474	        windowCurve = .allocate(capacity: Self.window)
475	        history = .allocate(capacity: Self.window)
476	        staging = .allocate(capacity: Self.hop)
477	        frame = .allocate(capacity: Self.window)
478	        real = .allocate(capacity: half)
479	        imaginary = .allocate(capacity: half)
480	        power = .allocate(capacity: half + 1)
481	        smoothed = .allocate(capacity: half + 1)
482	        minimum = .allocate(capacity: half + 1)
483	        binGain = .allocate(capacity: half + 1)
484	        cleaned = .allocate(capacity: half + 1)
485	        overlap = .allocate(capacity: Self.window)
486	        output = .allocate(capacity: Self.window + Self.hop)
487	
488	        history.initialize(repeating: 0, count: Self.window)
489	        staging.initialize(repeating: 0, count: Self.hop)
490	        frame.initialize(repeating: 0, count: Self.window)
491	        real.initialize(repeating: 0, count: half)
492	        imaginary.initialize(repeating: 0, count: half)
493	        power.initialize(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
494	        smoothed.initialize(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
495	        minimum.initialize(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
496	        binGain.initialize(repeating: 1, count: half + 1)
497	        cleaned.initialize(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
498	        overlap.initialize(repeating: 0, count: Self.window)
499	        output.initialize(repeating: 0, count: Self.window + Self.hop)
500	
501	        // Periodic Hann, square-rooted: `hann` itself is what the analysis and
502	        // synthesis windows multiply to, and 75 % overlap makes those sum to a
503	        // constant. The constant is computed rather than quoted, so the round
504	        // trip is unity whatever the window and hop become.
505	        var overlapSum: Float = 0
506	        for index in 0..<Self.window {
507	            let hann = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2 * Float.pi * Float(index) / Float(Self.window))
508	            windowCurve[index] = sqrt(max(hann, 0))
509	        }
510	        for step in stride(from: 0, to: Self.window, by: Self.hop) {
511	            let sample = windowCurve[step]
512	            overlapSum += sample * sample
513	        }
514	        // `vDSP_fft_zrip` returns a spectrum scaled by 2, and the inverse does
515	        // not undo the transform's own length, so a round trip needs 1/(2·N).
516	        scale = 1 / (2 * Float(Self.window) * max(overlapSum, .leastNormalMagnitude))
517	        resetState()
518	    }

520	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
521	        fatalError("AudioNoiseReductionStage does not support NSCoder")
522	    }

524	    deinit {
525	        vDSP_destroy_fftsetup(setup)
526	        windowCurve.deallocate()
527	        history.deallocate()
528	        staging.deallocate()
529	        frame.deallocate()
530	        real.deallocate()
531	        imaginary.deallocate()
532	        power.deallocate()
533	        smoothed.deallocate()
534	        minimum.deallocate()
535	        binGain.deallocate()
536	        cleaned.deallocate()
537	        overlap.deallocate()
538	        output.deallocate()

541	    /// Empties the pipeline and re-primes the delay line.
542	    ///
543	    /// The queue starts holding ONE HOP of silence, not one window. Frame `k`
544	    /// finishes the hop of output that begins at input `(k + 1)·hop − window`,
545	    /// so the overlap-add itself already delays by `window − hop`; priming the
546	    /// queue with one more hop makes the total exactly `window` and — checked
547	    /// against every arrival pattern, not just the tidy one — leaves the queue
548	    /// unable to run dry between hops.
549	    func reset() { resetState() }
550	
551	    private func resetState() {
552	        history.update(repeating: 0, count: Self.window)
553	        staging.update(repeating: 0, count: Self.hop)
554	        overlap.update(repeating: 0, count: Self.window)
555	        output.update(repeating: 0, count: Self.window + Self.hop)
556	        smoothed.update(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
557	        minimum.update(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
558	        cleaned.update(repeating: 0, count: half + 1)
559	        primed = false
560	        outputHead = 0
561	        outputTail = Self.hop
562	        stagedCount = 0
563	    }
564	
565	    /// Filters `frames` samples in place.
566	    ///
567	    /// `amount` is the clip's `noise_reduction`, read fresh on every call
568	    /// because the clip under the playhead changes at every cut. At 0 the
569	    /// gain floor is 1, every bin's gain is 1, and the stage is an exact
570	    /// (float-precision) delay rather than a filter — which is what keeps a
571	    /// track that mixes reduced and unreduced clips from changing its latency
572	    /// halfway through.
573	    func process(_ data: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>, frames: Int, amount: Double) {
574	        guard frames > 0 else { return }
575	        let clamped = Float(min(max(amount.isFinite ? amount : 0, 0), 1))
576	        // Over-subtraction: 1 removes exactly the estimate, 4 removes four
577	        // times it. The floor is what is left of a bin the subtraction would
578	        // otherwise empty; at amount 0 it is 1, which makes every gain 1.
579	        let overSubtraction = 1 + 3 * clamped
580	        let floorGain = 1 - clamped
581	
582	        for index in 0..<frames {
583	            // Samples are staged a hop at a time and the history is shifted
584	            // once per hop, not once per sample: the window is a plain
585	            // in-order buffer (which is what `vDSP_vmul` wants) and the price
586	            // of that is 384 floats moved per 128 samples rather than 511 per
587	            // one. A ring buffer would need no move at all and would cost an
588	            // unwrap on every read of every frame instead — the wrong trade at
589	            // 75 % overlap.
590	            staging[stagedCount] = data[index]
591	            stagedCount += 1
592	            if stagedCount == Self.hop {
593	                stagedCount = 0
594	                memmove(
595	                    history, history + Self.hop,
596	                    (Self.window - Self.hop) * MemoryLayout<Float>.size)
597	                (history + Self.window - Self.hop).update(from: staging, count: Self.hop)
598	                processFrame(overSubtraction: overSubtraction, floorGain: floorGain)
599	            }

600	            data[index] = popOutput()
601	        }
602	    }
603	
604	    /// One analysis/synthesis frame over the newest `window` samples.
605	    private func processFrame(overSubtraction: Float, floorGain: Float) {
606	        vDSP_vmul(history, 1, windowCurve, 1, frame, 1, vDSP_Length(Self.window))
607	
608	        var split = DSPSplitComplex(realp: real, imagp: imaginary)
609	        frame.withMemoryRebound(to: DSPComplex.self, capacity: half) { pointer in
610	            vDSP_ctoz(pointer, 2, &split, 1, vDSP_Length(half))
611	        }
612	        vDSP_fft_zrip(setup, &split, 1, log2n, FFTDirection(kFFTDirection_Forward))
613	
614	        // `vDSP_fft_zrip` packs DC in real[0] and Nyquist in imaginary[0];
615	        // both are real, so they get their own slots at either end of the
616	        // power array rather than being treated as a complex pair.
617	        power[0] = real[0] * real[0]
618	        power[half] = imaginary[0] * imaginary[0]
619	        for bin in 1..<half {
620	            power[bin] = real[bin] * real[bin] + imaginary[bin] * imaginary[bin]
621	        }
622	
623	        for bin in 0...half {
624	            let current = power[bin]
625	            let smooth =
626	                primed ? powerSmoothing * smoothed[bin] + (1 - powerSmoothing) * current : current
627	            if !primed {
628	                minimum[bin] = smooth
629	            } else if minimum[bin] < smooth {
630	                // Rise slowly, and only as fast as the smoothed power itself
631	                // is rising — Doblinger's recursion, which is what stops a
632	                // long vowel from dragging the floor up with it.
633	                minimum[bin] =
634	                    minimumRise * minimum[bin]
635	                    + ((1 - minimumRise) / (1 - minimumBias))
636	                    * (smooth - minimumBias * smoothed[bin])
637	            } else {
638	                minimum[bin] = smooth
639	            }
640	            smoothed[bin] = smooth
641	
642	            // The gain is a Wiener filter over the a priori SNR, and the a
643	            // priori SNR is the decision-directed estimate: mostly what last
644	            // frame's clean output says this bin holds, corrected by what
645	            // this frame's power says. Subtracting the noise estimate from
646	            // the power directly (the textbook subtractor) makes the gain
647	            // jump with the periodogram's own variance, which is heard as
648	            // bins winking in and out; this does not.
649	            let noise = max(max(minimum[bin], 0) * noiseBias, .leastNormalMagnitude)
650	            let posterior = current / noise
651	            let prior = max(
652	                decisionDirected * cleaned[bin] / noise
653	                    + (1 - decisionDirected) * max(posterior - 1, 0),
654	                1e-6)
655	            // `overSubtraction` in the denominator generalises the filter: 1
656	            // is the plain Wiener gain, 4 removes four times as much for the
657	            // same SNR. The floor is what a bin keeps when the filter would
658	            // otherwise empty it — at amount 0 the floor is 1 and the whole
659	            // rule collapses to a no-op.
660	            let gain = max(floorGain, prior / (prior + overSubtraction))
661	            binGain[bin] = gain
662	            cleaned[bin] = gain * gain * current
663	        }
664	        primed = true
665	
666	        real[0] *= binGain[0]
667	        imaginary[0] *= binGain[half]
668	        for bin in 1..<half {
669	            real[bin] *= binGain[bin]
670	            imaginary[bin] *= binGain[bin]
671	        }
672	
673	        vDSP_fft_zrip(setup, &split, 1, log2n, FFTDirection(kFFTDirection_Inverse))
674	        frame.withMemoryRebound(to: DSPComplex.self, capacity: half) { pointer in
675	            vDSP_ztoc(&split, 1, pointer, 2, vDSP_Length(half))
676	        }
677	        var factor = scale
678	        vDSP_vsmul(frame, 1, &factor, frame, 1, vDSP_Length(Self.window))
679	        vDSP_vmul(frame, 1, windowCurve, 1, frame, 1, vDSP_Length(Self.window))
680	        vDSP_vadd(overlap, 1, frame, 1, overlap, 1, vDSP_Length(Self.window))
681	
682	        // The first `hop` samples of the accumulator have now been summed by
683	        // every frame that covers them, so they are finished: they go to the
684	        // output queue and the accumulator slides.
685	        pushOutput(overlap, count: Self.hop)
686	        memmove(overlap, overlap + Self.hop, (Self.window - Self.hop) * MemoryLayout<Float>.size)
687	        (overlap + Self.window - Self.hop).update(repeating: 0, count: Self.hop)
688	    }
689	
690	    /// Appends finished samples, compacting the queue first when the tail has
691	    /// run out of room. The queue holds at most two hops, so the capacity of
692	    /// `window + hop` can never actually be exceeded; the `take` clamp is
693	    /// there so that a future window/hop pair which broke that invariant would
694	    /// drop samples rather than write off the end.
695	    private func pushOutput(_ source: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>, count: Int) {
696	        let capacity = Self.window + Self.hop
697	        if outputTail + count > capacity {
698	            let held = outputTail - outputHead
699	            if held > 0 { memmove(output, output + outputHead, held * MemoryLayout<Float>.size) }
700	            outputHead = 0
701	            outputTail = held
702	        }
703	        let take = min(count, capacity - outputTail)
704	        guard take > 0 else { return }
705	        (output + outputTail).update(from: source, count: take)
706	        outputTail += take
707	    }
708	
709	    private func popOutput() -> Float {
710	        guard outputHead < outputTail else { return 0 }
711	        let value = output[outputHead]
712	        outputHead += 1
713	        return value
714	    }
715	}

719	/// One composition audio track's effect chain: noise reduction, then the
720	/// compressor, then the Mix stage — the mono fold, then the pan, then the
721	/// fold an enclosing NEST clip asked for.
722	///
723	/// **That order is the order a channel strip has**, and each step is there
724	/// because of the one before it. Cleaning first means the compressor is not
725	/// asked to make a decision about a level the hiss is holding up — a
726	/// compressor in front of a noise reducer pumps the noise floor audibly.
727	/// Panning last means the reduction is computed on the signal as it was
728	/// recorded, not on a channel the pan has already leaned.
729	///
730	/// **The fold is at the head of the Mix stage, after the compressor and
731	/// before the pan.** After the pan it would undo it (see `AudioPanLaw`);
732	/// before the noise reducer it would hand both reducers identical input,
733	/// which invites the false optimisation of running one and copying — and a
734	/// stage that stopped being fed would click the moment mono came off at a
735	/// cut, because mono is a per-CLIP setting and the reducers are stateful.
736	/// Where it is, it also makes `AudioPane`'s Mix section — which holds `mono`
737	/// and `pan`, in that order — literally the DSP order, which that pane
738	/// already claims for the other three sections.
739	///
740	/// **A NEST clip's fold is the one thing that runs after the pan**, and it is
741	/// not an exception to the paragraph above: it belongs to a different clip.
742	/// It stands for a fold of the whole nest's MIX, and a mix is a sum, so
743	/// folding each contributor at the very end of its own chain sums to exactly
744	/// the same samples (`AudioClipDSP.enclosingMono` argues it). Running it at
745	/// the head with the clip's own would fold BEFORE the inner clip's pan and
746	/// leave a hard-panned clip hard-panned inside a nest the user folded.
747	///
748	/// The clip's own volume, its fades and any ducking are NOT here: `audio.rs`
749	/// folds those into the plan's envelope and `AVMutableAudioMixInputParameters`
750	/// applies them as volume ramps, which — measured — happen downstream of a
751	/// tap created with `kMTAudioProcessingTapCreationFlag_PreEffects`. So the
752	/// full order the samples actually see is
753	/// noise reduction → compressor → the clip's fold → pan → an enclosing nest's
754	/// fold → volume/fades/ducking, which puts the compressor before the fader
755	/// exactly as an insert should be.
756	final class AudioDSPChain {
757	    let channelCount: Int
758	    private let compressor: AudioCompressorStage
759	    /// One per channel, or nil when no clip on this track asks for noise
760	    /// reduction — in which case the track has no added latency at all.
761	    private let reducers: [AudioNoiseReductionStage]?
762	
763	    /// `usesNoiseReduction` is decided for the WHOLE track when the
764	    /// composition is built, not per buffer: the stage adds a fixed delay, and
765	    /// switching it in and out at a cut would make the track jump backwards
766	    /// and forwards by 10 ms.
767	    init(channelCount: Int, sampleRate: Double, maxFrames: Int, usesNoiseReduction: Bool) {
768	        self.channelCount = max(0, channelCount)
769	        compressor = AudioCompressorStage(sampleRate: sampleRate, maxFrames: maxFrames)
770	        if usesNoiseReduction, self.channelCount > 0 {
771	            // All channels or none: a track whose left channel was filtered
772	            // and whose right was not would be delayed on one side, which is
773	            // worse than not filtering at all. `vDSP_create_fftsetup` is the
774	            // only thing that can fail here, and if it does the clip plays
775	            // and exports with its pan and compressor and without its noise
776	            // reduction, rather than not playing.
777	            let stages = (0..<self.channelCount).compactMap { _ in AudioNoiseReductionStage() }
778	            reducers = stages.count == self.channelCount ? stages : nil
779	        } else {
780	            reducers = nil
781	        }
782	    }
783	
784	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
785	        fatalError("AudioDSPChain does not support NSCoder")
786	    }
787	
788	    /// Drops every bit of carried state — the compressor's envelope, the
789	    /// reducers' delay lines and noise estimates. `AudioTap` calls this when
790	    /// the stream restarts, so a seek does not play the previous position's
791	    /// tail.
792	    func reset() {
793	        compressor.reset()
794	        reducers?.forEach { $0.reset() }
795	    }
796	
797	    /// Runs the chain in place over one buffer.
798	    ///
799	    /// `params` is the clip under this buffer's timestamp. It changes at every
800	    /// cut on the track; the stages carry their state across the change, which
801	    /// is what a track insert does.
802	    func process(
803	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, frames: Int,
804	        params: AudioClipDSP
805	    ) {
806	        let count = min(channels.count, channelCount)
807	        guard frames > 0, count > 0 else { return }
808	
809	        if let reducers = reducers {
810	            for channel in 0..<min(count, reducers.count) {
811	                guard let data = channels[channel] else { continue }
812	                reducers[channel].process(data, frames: frames, amount: params.noiseReduction)
813	            }
814	        }
815	
816	        compressor.process(channels, count: count, frames: frames, settings: params.compressor)
817	
818	        // The head of the Mix stage. The branch is not entered at all for a
819	        // clip that does not ask for mono — not multiplied by one, not folded
820	        // with a weight of zero — which is what makes an untouched track's
821	        // samples bit-identical to the build before this landed, by
822	        // construction rather than by argument.
823	        if params.mono, count >= 2 { fold(channels, count: count, frames: frames) }
824	
825	        pan(channels, count: count, frames: frames, position: params.pan)
826	
827	        // The tail: the fold a nest clip ABOVE this one asked for, after
828	        // everything this clip does to its own channels, which is what makes
829	        // the sum of the folded contributors the fold of the sum.
830	        if params.enclosingMono, count >= 2 { fold(channels, count: count, frames: frames) }
831	    }
832	
833	    /// The pan, in place. Its own method only so the tail fold above it is
834	    /// reachable: every early return here used to end `process`.
835	    ///
836	    /// Pan needs somewhere to pan TO. A mono composition track is prepared
837	    /// with one channel and is widened to stereo downstream of the tap, so
838	    /// there is nothing here to lean; the pan is silently inaudible on such a
839	    /// clip rather than turning into a volume change, which is what applying
840	    /// half a pan law to a single channel would be.
841	    private func pan(
842	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, count: Int,
843	        frames: Int, position: Double
844	    ) {
845	        guard count >= 2 else { return }
846	        let gains = AudioPanLaw.gains(position)
847	        guard gains.left != 1 || gains.right != 1 else { return }
848	        var left = gains.left
849	        var right = gains.right
850	        if let data = channels[0] { vDSP_vsmul(data, 1, &left, data, 1, vDSP_Length(frames)) }
851	        if let data = channels[1] { vDSP_vsmul(data, 1, &right, data, 1, vDSP_Length(frames)) }
852	    }
853	
854	    /// Averages EVERY channel and writes the average to all of them.
855	    ///
856	    /// **Every channel, not L and R.** `prepare` is handed the COMPOSITION
857	    /// track's channel count, so a 5.1 source gives 6; folding only channels 0
858	    /// and 1 would leave four untouched and produce something that is neither
859	    /// mono nor the original. At two channels this is exactly (L+R)/2.
860	    ///
861	    /// Allocation-free and stateless: `count` linear passes plus `count − 1`
862	    /// copies over at most `maxFrames` floats, which is two orders of
863	    /// magnitude under one noise-reduction frame. The accumulator is the first
864	    /// channel that actually has a buffer, and the divisor counts only the
865	    /// channels that contributed — a null buffer must not quietly attenuate
866	    /// the rest.
867	    private func fold(
868	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, count: Int,
869	        frames: Int
870	    ) {
871	        var accumulator: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?
872	        var summed = 0
873	        for channel in 0..<count {
874	            guard let data = channels[channel] else { continue }
875	            summed += 1
876	            guard let into = accumulator else {
877	                accumulator = data
878	                continue
879	            }
880	            vDSP_vadd(into, 1, data, 1, into, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
881	        }
882	        guard let into = accumulator, summed >= 2 else { return }
883	        var scale = 1 / Float(summed)
884	        vDSP_vsmul(into, 1, &scale, into, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
885	        for channel in 0..<count {
886	            guard let data = channels[channel], data != into else { continue }
887	            data.update(from: into, count: frames)
888	        }
889	    }
890	}

600	            data[index] = popOutput()
601	        }
602	    }

692	    /// `window + hop` can never actually be exceeded; the `take` clamp is
693	    /// there so that a future window/hop pair which broke that invariant would
694	    /// drop samples rather than write off the end.
695	    private func pushOutput(_ source: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>, count: Int) {
696	        let capacity = Self.window + Self.hop
697	        if outputTail + count > capacity {
698	            let held = outputTail - outputHead
699	            if held > 0 { memmove(output, output + outputHead, held * MemoryLayout<Float>.size) }
700	            outputHead = 0
701	            outputTail = held
702	        }
703	        let take = min(count, capacity - outputTail)
704	        guard take > 0 else { return }
705	        (output + outputTail).update(from: source, count: take)
706	        outputTail += take
707	    }
708	
709	    private func popOutput() -> Float {
710	        guard outputHead < outputTail else { return 0 }
711	        let value = output[outputHead]
712	        outputHead += 1
713	        return value
714	    }
715	}
716	
717	// MARK: - The chain
718	
719	/// One composition audio track's effect chain: noise reduction, then the
720	/// compressor, then the Mix stage — the mono fold, then the pan, then the
721	/// fold an enclosing NEST clip asked for.
722	///
723	/// **That order is the order a channel strip has**, and each step is there
724	/// because of the one before it. Cleaning first means the compressor is not
725	/// asked to make a decision about a level the hiss is holding up — a
726	/// compressor in front of a noise reducer pumps the noise floor audibly.
727	/// Panning last means the reduction is computed on the signal as it was
728	/// recorded, not on a channel the pan has already leaned.
729	///
730	/// **The fold is at the head of the Mix stage, after the compressor and
731	/// before the pan.** After the pan it would undo it (see `AudioPanLaw`);
732	/// before the noise reducer it would hand both reducers identical input,
733	/// which invites the false optimisation of running one and copying — and a
734	/// stage that stopped being fed would click the moment mono came off at a
735	/// cut, because mono is a per-CLIP setting and the reducers are stateful.
736	/// Where it is, it also makes `AudioPane`'s Mix section — which holds `mono`
737	/// and `pan`, in that order — literally the DSP order, which that pane
738	/// already claims for the other three sections.
739	///
740	/// **A NEST clip's fold is the one thing that runs after the pan**, and it is
741	/// not an exception to the paragraph above: it belongs to a different clip.
742	/// It stands for a fold of the whole nest's MIX, and a mix is a sum, so
743	/// folding each contributor at the very end of its own chain sums to exactly
744	/// the same samples (`AudioClipDSP.enclosingMono` argues it). Running it at
745	/// the head with the clip's own would fold BEFORE the inner clip's pan and
746	/// leave a hard-panned clip hard-panned inside a nest the user folded.
747	///
748	/// The clip's own volume, its fades and any ducking are NOT here: `audio.rs`
749	/// folds those into the plan's envelope and `AVMutableAudioMixInputParameters`
750	/// applies them as volume ramps, which — measured — happen downstream of a
751	/// tap created with `kMTAudioProcessingTapCreationFlag_PreEffects`. So the
752	/// full order the samples actually see is
753	/// noise reduction → compressor → the clip's fold → pan → an enclosing nest's
754	/// fold → volume/fades/ducking, which puts the compressor before the fader
755	/// exactly as an insert should be.
756	final class AudioDSPChain {
757	    let channelCount: Int
758	    private let compressor: AudioCompressorStage
759	    /// One per channel, or nil when no clip on this track asks for noise
760	    /// reduction — in which case the track has no added latency at all.
761	    private let reducers: [AudioNoiseReductionStage]?
762	
763	    /// `usesNoiseReduction` is decided for the WHOLE track when the
764	    /// composition is built, not per buffer: the stage adds a fixed delay, and
765	    /// switching it in and out at a cut would make the track jump backwards
766	    /// and forwards by 10 ms.
767	    init(channelCount: Int, sampleRate: Double, maxFrames: Int, usesNoiseReduction: Bool) {
768	        self.channelCount = max(0, channelCount)
769	        compressor = AudioCompressorStage(sampleRate: sampleRate, maxFrames: maxFrames)
770	        if usesNoiseReduction, self.channelCount > 0 {
771	            // All channels or none: a track whose left channel was filtered
772	            // and whose right was not would be delayed on one side, which is
773	            // worse than not filtering at all. `vDSP_create_fftsetup` is the
774	            // only thing that can fail here, and if it does the clip plays
775	            // and exports with its pan and compressor and without its noise
776	            // reduction, rather than not playing.
777	            let stages = (0..<self.channelCount).compactMap { _ in AudioNoiseReductionStage() }
778	            reducers = stages.count == self.channelCount ? stages : nil
779	        } else {
780	            reducers = nil
781	        }
782	    }
783	
784	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
785	        fatalError("AudioDSPChain does not support NSCoder")
786	    }
787	
788	    /// Drops every bit of carried state — the compressor's envelope, the
789	    /// reducers' delay lines and noise estimates. `AudioTap` calls this when
790	    /// the stream restarts, so a seek does not play the previous position's
791	    /// tail.
792	    func reset() {
793	        compressor.reset()
794	        reducers?.forEach { $0.reset() }
795	    }
796	
797	    /// Runs the chain in place over one buffer.
798	    ///
799	    /// `params` is the clip under this buffer's timestamp. It changes at every
800	    /// cut on the track; the stages carry their state across the change, which
801	    /// is what a track insert does.
802	    func process(
803	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, frames: Int,
804	        params: AudioClipDSP
805	    ) {
806	        let count = min(channels.count, channelCount)
807	        guard frames > 0, count > 0 else { return }
808	
809	        if let reducers = reducers {
810	            for channel in 0..<min(count, reducers.count) {
811	                guard let data = channels[channel] else { continue }
812	                reducers[channel].process(data, frames: frames, amount: params.noiseReduction)
813	            }
814	        }
815	
816	        compressor.process(channels, count: count, frames: frames, settings: params.compressor)
817	
818	        // The head of the Mix stage. The branch is not entered at all for a
819	        // clip that does not ask for mono — not multiplied by one, not folded
820	        // with a weight of zero — which is what makes an untouched track's
821	        // samples bit-identical to the build before this landed, by
822	        // construction rather than by argument.
823	        if params.mono, count >= 2 { fold(channels, count: count, frames: frames) }
824	
825	        pan(channels, count: count, frames: frames, position: params.pan)
826	
827	        // The tail: the fold a nest clip ABOVE this one asked for, after
828	        // everything this clip does to its own channels, which is what makes
829	        // the sum of the folded contributors the fold of the sum.
830	        if params.enclosingMono, count >= 2 { fold(channels, count: count, frames: frames) }
831	    }
832	
833	    /// The pan, in place. Its own method only so the tail fold above it is
834	    /// reachable: every early return here used to end `process`.
835	    ///
836	    /// Pan needs somewhere to pan TO. A mono composition track is prepared
837	    /// with one channel and is widened to stereo downstream of the tap, so
838	    /// there is nothing here to lean; the pan is silently inaudible on such a
839	    /// clip rather than turning into a volume change, which is what applying
840	    /// half a pan law to a single channel would be.
841	    private func pan(
842	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, count: Int,
843	        frames: Int, position: Double
844	    ) {
845	        guard count >= 2 else { return }
846	        let gains = AudioPanLaw.gains(position)
847	        guard gains.left != 1 || gains.right != 1 else { return }
848	        var left = gains.left
849	        var right = gains.right
850	        if let data = channels[0] { vDSP_vsmul(data, 1, &left, data, 1, vDSP_Length(frames)) }
851	        if let data = channels[1] { vDSP_vsmul(data, 1, &right, data, 1, vDSP_Length(frames)) }
852	    }
853	
854	    /// Averages EVERY channel and writes the average to all of them.
855	    ///
856	    /// **Every channel, not L and R.** `prepare` is handed the COMPOSITION
857	    /// track's channel count, so a 5.1 source gives 6; folding only channels 0
858	    /// and 1 would leave four untouched and produce something that is neither
859	    /// mono nor the original. At two channels this is exactly (L+R)/2.
860	    ///
861	    /// Allocation-free and stateless: `count` linear passes plus `count − 1`
862	    /// copies over at most `maxFrames` floats, which is two orders of
863	    /// magnitude under one noise-reduction frame. The accumulator is the first
864	    /// channel that actually has a buffer, and the divisor counts only the
865	    /// channels that contributed — a null buffer must not quietly attenuate
866	    /// the rest.
867	    private func fold(
868	        _ channels: UnsafeMutableBufferPointer<UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?>, count: Int,
869	        frames: Int
870	    ) {
871	        var accumulator: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?
872	        var summed = 0
873	        for channel in 0..<count {
874	            guard let data = channels[channel] else { continue }
875	            summed += 1
876	            guard let into = accumulator else {
877	                accumulator = data
878	                continue
879	            }
880	            vDSP_vadd(into, 1, data, 1, into, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
881	        }
882	        guard let into = accumulator, summed >= 2 else { return }
883	        var scale = 1 / Float(summed)
884	        vDSP_vsmul(into, 1, &scale, into, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
885	        for channel in 0..<count {
886	            guard let data = channels[channel], data != into else { continue }
887	            data.update(from: into, count: frames)
888	        }
889	    }
890	}
